title: Tenant-scoped Audit Orchestrator for Policy-as-Code & Drift Healing
creator: Ravi Patel
description: Build an orchestrator service that enforces tenant-scoped policy-as-code for data residency and retention settings, continuously detects config drift across Hosted/Dedicated/Private deployments, and performs automated remediation or staged healing with audit evidence. The service should emit tamper-evident evidence bundles tied to customer tenancy, integrate with the Console for visibility (per-tenant dashboards), surface actionable signals for SRE/CS, and support safe rollbacks and manual overrides. This ticket covers the core engine, policy packaging, drift detectors, a remediation runner with approval gates, and the initial Console integration.
acceptance_criteria: Agent can evaluate policy bundles (Rego or in-house DSL) against tenant config snapshots and produce deterministic pass/fail with lineage metadata
Drift detector runs on a schedule and identifies divergence between configured retention/residency policies and actual runtime/app config for 95% of sampled tenants in staging
Remediation runner can perform read-only dry-run + optional auto-apply for low-risk fixes (label sync, TTL adjustments) and create an evidence bundle with config diff + applied command logs
Console shows per-tenant drift score, last-evidence timestamp, and provides a one-click approve/rollback flow for remediation actions

End-to-end test harness and CI job validate drift detection and remediation against a matrix of 12 simulated misconfigurations (region mismatch, TTL absent, bucket-level retention mismatch, export endpoints enabled)
implementation_notes: Core components: (1) policy-evaluator microservice that compiles policy bundles to WASM (or OPA) for fast multi-tenant evaluation; (2) snapshotter that aggregates residency/retention surface area (control-plane configs, storage/ingress configs, runtime policies) into signed JSON blobs; (3) drift-detector comparing desired vs observed with fuzzy matching rules for semantically equivalent configs; (4) remediation-runner with idempotent inspectors and action adapters for Console, Terraform state, and infra provisioning APIs; (5) evidence-exporter that signs and stores artifacts to an immutable store and creates links for auditing. Use existing logging/tracing libraries, and ensure all actions are logged with request-id and operator principal. Consider policy packaging format so customers can supply custom tenant policies via their org settings.
rollout_plan: MVP in staging: enable evaluation and dry-run remediation on 50 internal test tenants
Beta: invite 3 pilot customers on Dedicated to opt into automated detection with manual remediation workflow
Gradual ramp: enable auto-apply for low-risk fixes for non-production tenants after 3 weeks of pilot stability
GA: enable for all Hosted tiers with documentation and opt-out controls; add an opt-in flag for Private deployments
monitoring_and_metrics: time_to_detect_ms and time_to_remediate_ms (SLO targets: detect < 10m for config-change triggers, remediate < 30m for auto-applies)
alert: sustained drift > 5% of tenants in a region for 1h
risks_and_tradeoffs: Automatic remediation reduces toil but increases blast radius if policy tooling is incorrect. Trade-offs: rely on dry-run + approval gates for high-impact changes; allow per-tenant opt-out and safe-lists. Implementation choice: compile policies to WASM for performance vs Rego/OPA for familiarity — choose WASM compilation with shim adapter for existing Rego rules to get performance while keeping policy author ergonomics. Storing signed evidence increases storage costs; retain summarized evidence for 90 days and full artifacts for 1 year for enterprise customers.
security_considerations: All snapshots and evidence bundles must be encrypted at rest and signed. Remediation-runner must honor RBAC and require a service principal with least privilege. For Private deployments, support local KMS integration and ensure evidence export never crosses tenant boundaries. Security review required before GA. Include mitigations for replay attacks on evidence bundles by including monotonic sequence numbers and timestamp + canonical signer metadata.
